AuthRequirement,\n) -> Result<String, auth::AuthError> {\n    let token = extract_auth_token(req).ok_or(auth::AuthError::Unauthorized)?;\n    let (username, role) = auth::verify_bearer(token, users)?;\n    match requirement {\n        AuthRequirement::Any => Ok(username),\n        AuthRequirement::Dm if role == \"dm\" => Ok(username),\n        AuthRequirement::Player if role == \"player\" => Ok(username),\n        _ => Err(auth::AuthError::Forbidden),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse one HTTP request, route it, and write the response.\n///\n/// Both in-memory state maps are locked for the duration of the request so that\n/// reads and writes are serialized and persistence is consistent.\nfn dispatch_request(stream: &mut TcpStream) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    let req = read_request(stream)?;\n    let first = req.lines().next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let parts: Vec<&str> = first.split_whitespace().collect();\n    if parts.len() < 2 {\n        return respond(stream, 400, BAD_REQUEST);\n    }\n    let method = parts[0];\n    let path = parts[1];\n    let body = extract_body(&req);\n\n    let mut sessions = SESSIONS.lock().unwrap();\n    let mut users = USERS.lock().unwrap();\n\n    let (status, response) = match method {\n        \"GET\" => dispatch_get(path, &req, &sessions, &users),\n        \"POST\" => dispatch_post(path, body, &req, &mut sessions, &mut users),\n        \"PUT\" => dispatch_put(path, body, &req, &mut sessions, &mut users),\n        \"DELETE\" => dispatch_delete(path, body, &req, &mut sessions, &mut users),\n        _ => (404, NOT_FOUND.to_string()),\n    };\n    respond(stream, status, &response)\n}\n\n/// Return the body portion of a fully read HTTP request.\nfn extract_body(req: &str) -> &str {\n    if let Some(pos) = req.find(\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\") {\n        &req[pos + 4..]\n    } else {\n        \"\"\n    }\n}\n\n/// Dispatch GET requests.\nfn dispatch_get(\n    path: &str,\n    req: &str,\n    _sessions:  let _ = save_storage(sessions, users);\n                (201, resp)\n            }\n            Err(auth::RegisterError::Conflict) => {\n                (409, r#\"{\"error\":\"duplicate play_campaign_owner_status(campaign_id).map_err(|_| PlayError::BadRequest)?;\n    if owner != actor {\n        return Err(PlayError::Conflict);\n    }\n    let (current_actor, phase, turn_number) =\n        play_campaign_get_turn(campaign_id).map_err(|_| PlayError::BadRequest)?;\n    if current_actor != \"dm\" || (phase != \"dm\" && phase != \"exploration\") {\n        return escape_json(&next_actor),\n        new_turn_number\n    ))\n}\n\n/// Parse a play campaign scene sub-resource path.\n///\n/// For example, `/v1/play/campaigns/{id}/scenes/{scene_id}/enter` `\"status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'healthy'\"`. This is used by the startup\n/// migrations to make older schemas forward-compatible without altering\n/// behavior for newly created databases.\nfn add_column_if_missing(table: &str, column: &str, definition: &str) -> Result<(), String> {\n    let sql = format!(\"PRAGMA table_info({});\", table);\n    let output = sqlite_query(&sql)?;\n\n    let content = extract_top_array_content(&output).unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let has_column = extract_objects(content)\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter_map(|o| extract_string(o, \"name\"))\n        .any(|name| name == column);\n    if !has_column {\n        sqlite_exec(&format!(\"ALTER TABLE {} ADD COLUMN {};\", table, definition))?;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Add missing death-save columns to an existing play_campaign_members table.\n///\n/// Older schemas created before the death-saves stage lack `status`,\n/// `death_saves_successes`, and `death_saves_failures`. `\"status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'healthy'\"`. This is used by the startup\n/// migrations to make older schemas forward-compatible without altering\n/// behavior for newly created databases.\nfn add_column_if_missing(table: &str, column: &str, definition: &str) -> Result<(), String> {\n    let sql = format!(\"PRAGMA table_info({});\", table);\n    let output = sqlite_query(&sql)?;\n\n    let content = extract_top_array_content(&output).unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let has_column = extract_objects(content)\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter_map(|o| extract_string(o, \"name\"))\n        .any(|name| name == column);\n    if !has_column {\n        sqlite_exec(&format!(\"ALTER TABLE {} ADD COLUMN {};\", table, definition))?;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Add missing death-save columns to an existing play_campaign_members table.\n///\n/// Older schemas created before the death-saves stage lack `status`,\n/// `death_saves_successes`, and `death_saves_failures`. Each\n/// key must be a double-quoted string, followed by a colon, followed by an\n/// integer (optional leading `-`). Whitespace around punctuation is allowed.\npub fn extract_int_object(text: &str, key: &str) -> Option<Vec<(String, i64)>> {\n    let content = extract_object_content(text, key)?;\n    let mut result = Vec::new();\n    let mut rest = content.trim_start();\n    while !rest.is_empty() {\n        rest = rest.trim_start();\n        if !rest.starts_with('\"') {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let inner = &rest[1..];\n        let end = inner.find('\"')?;\n        let key = inner[..end].to_string();\n        rest = &inner[end + 1..];\n        rest = rest.trim_start();\n        if !rest.starts_with(':') {\n            return None;\n        }\n        rest = &rest[1..].trim_start();\n        let num_start = rest.find(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '-')?;\n        rest = &rest[num_start..];\n        let num_end = rest.find(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit() && c != '-').unwrap_or(rest.len());\n        let num_str = &rest[..num_end];\n        if num_str.is_empty() || num_str == \"-\" {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let value: i64 = num_str.parse().ok()?;\n        result.push((key, value));\n        rest = &rest[num_end..].trim_start();\n        if rest.is_empty() {\n            break;\n        }\n        if !rest.starts_with(',') {\n            return None;\n        }\n        rest = &rest[1..];\n    }\n    Some(result)\n}\n```\n\nWait, there's a potential issue: `rest.find(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '-')` will find the first digit or minus.
